citations.claim: energy exceeds allowed 3324.78 at first violating step
post-bounce outbound speed higher than inbound despite no work input

counterfactual.change: Changed restitution e from 0.907 to 0.0 (single field); inelastic bounce removes energy gain so violation disappears

explanation: Shrunk scenario is single ball dropping to floor (y=0) with e≈0.907, no controller. At step 60 it approaches floor with speed 18.67 and energy ~3017 (near E0). Bounce at step 60->61 reverses vy to +19.73, energy jumps to 3363 exceeding allowed 3324. The restitution impulse is not energy-conserving in combination with gravity substepping/position correction, adding ~346 J in one bounce. Setting e=0 makes it inelastic so no energy gain.
vision_note: Across steps 58-60 the single blue ball drops toward the floor and contacts it at step 60-61, then immediately rebounds upward. No walls, controller, or other bodies are visible and the ball appears to leave the floor faster than it approached, consistent with an energetic bounce rather than settling.
